metadata.title: Neural Fitted Q Iteration - First Experiences with a Data Efficient Neural Reinforcement Learning Method (Riedmiller, 2005)
metadata.framework: Batch Q-learning with neural network function approximation using collected experience sets
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Riedmiller (2005). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: Batch Q-learning framework
nodes.statement: Collect a set of experience tuples $\mathcal{D} = \{(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)\}_{i=1}^{N}$ (state, action, reward, next state). Learn the Q-function $Q(s, a)$ offline from this fixed batch of transitions, rather than learning online as transitions are collected.

nodes.name: Neural Fitted Q Iteration (NFQ)
nodes.statement: At each iteration $k$: (1) For each transition $(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i) \in \mathcal{D}$, compute target $y_i = r_i + \gamma \max_{a'} Q_k(s'_i, a')$ using the current network $Q_k$. (2) Train a new neural network $Q_{k+1}$ from scratch on the training set $\{((s_i, a_i), y_i)\}$ using supervised learning (Rprop optimizer). Iterate until convergence.

nodes.name: Neural network architecture for NFQ
nodes.statement: A multilayer perceptron taking state-action pair $(s, a)$ as input and outputting a single Q-value estimate. Typically 2-3 hidden layers with 20-50 units each. The network is retrained from random initialization at each fitted Q iteration.

nodes.name: NFQ algorithm
nodes.statement: Input: experience set $\mathcal{D}$, discount $\gamma$. Initialize $Q_0$ randomly. Repeat for $k = 0, 1, \ldots$: (1) Generate pattern set $\mathcal{P} = \{((s_i, a_i), r_i + \gamma \max_{a'} Q_k(s'_i, a'))\}$. (2) Train neural network $Q_{k+1}$ on $\mathcal{P}$ using Rprop to convergence. Until Q-values stabilize.

nodes.name: Data efficiency
nodes.statement: NFQ is highly data-efficient: it reuses the entire experience set at each iteration. On the cart-pole swing-up task, NFQ learns a successful policy from only ~100 episodes of experience.

nodes.name: Batch vs. online learning
nodes.statement: Unlike online Q-learning which updates after each transition, NFQ collects all experiences first and then performs multiple passes of fitted Q iteration. This batch approach avoids issues with non-stationary targets during online learning but requires storing all transitions.
